name: tavrik
author: rule-family designer (world: 4-7 letter common English words; lineup answer, revision 4)
description:
WORD RULE-FAMILY class, REVISION 4 (docs/RULE_FAMILIES.md sec. "Revision 3" and its addenda; full tables in challenges/lab/NOTES_rules_words.md sec. 25-30; v1/v2/v3 kept as challenges/lab/tavrik.v1.json, tavrik.v2.json, tavrik.v3.json). World = 4-7 letter common English words. CLUE = the MINIMAL identifying example set, almost always TWO words (2 examples 98.8 %, 3 examples 1.2 % over 2000 seeds), one per line, lowercase; then a BLANK LINE; then FIVE candidate words, one per line, all real words of the same length as each other. ANSWER = the one candidate that obeys the hidden rule, written back verbatim (case- and whitespace-insensitive) or as its 1-based index 1..5. Exactly one candidate obeys the rule (verified in generate on every clue), so the floor is 1/5 = 20 %.
WHAT REVISION 4 IS. A TRIM OF v3 FOR KID LEGIBILITY, not a rebuild: same world, same lineup machinery, same 627-predicate attacker bank, same levers. v3 measured 45 / 42 / 47 / 24 % across four demo-less Opus centaurs (39 % overall, inside the 35-55 band) but the judge scored it kid 3.83: "half the universe reads like a puzzle-book trick (alphabet-distance, 2nd==2nd-from-last, comes-back-after-n-letters) rather than a playground observation; trim toward templates a kid spots by eye without counting". So EVERY COUNTED RELATION IS RETIRED to the trap list: "the first and last letters are exactly n apart in the alphabet" (v3 T0, four rules), "a letter comes back after exactly one / two other letters" (v3 T1, T2), and the four alphabet SCANS "the first / last letter is the earliest / latest in the alphabet of all its letters" (v3 T4-T7), which need a kid to sort seven letters. Eleven of v3's 41 rules go. Two relations are added in their place that a kid checks with one look -- "the same letter starts and ends it" and "the same consonant turns up twice" -- and the rule the judge explicitly blessed, "the 2nd letter and the 2nd-from-last letter are the same", stays. Nothing in U now contains a count, a distance, a sum or an alphabet scan.
THE UNIVERSE U: 13 templates, 33 rules, an ANTICHAIN verified by brute force over the 4412-word example pool AND over all 56176 dictionary words of length 4-7 (0 nesting violations; every rule has >= 1592 dictionary instances). Read them all aloud: (0) the 2nd letter and the 2nd-from-last letter are the same [density .073 in the dictionary, best Jaccard against the 627-predicate bank .19]; (1) the back half has more vowels than the front half [.251, .34]; (2) the front half has more vowels than the back half [.184, .49]; (3) the first vowel is an a/e/i/o/u [.140-.299, .47-.75]; (4) the last vowel is an a/i/o/u [.082-.241, .41-.53]; (5) the same vowel turns up twice [.328, .53]; (6) the same consonant turns up twice [.292, .60]; (7) the vowels go up the alphabet [.346, .50]; (8) the vowels go down the alphabet [.418, .58]; and the FOUR templates a generic word-predicate bank already holds [Jaccard 1.00], kept on purpose as the LEARNABLE SLOPE: (9) the same letter starts and ends it [.046]; (10) there is a b/f/k/m/p/v/w in it [.055-.176]; (11) it has a double letter [.170]; (12) it ends with d/g/l/n/r/s/t/y [.028-.116]. Mean density of the hidden rule 0.184; template mix over 500 clues 5.2-10.0 % each. The four slope templates take 30 % of clues at the plain one-slot-per-template draw -- the ~25 % the recipe asks for -- and the simulated attack scores 90-100 % on them against 33 % on the nine relations. A v3-style DOUBLE draw weight for three cheap templates was measured at 58.1 % vs 47.4 % at 60 labels, off the top of the band, so the doubling is spent on having a fourth cheap template instead of on drawing three of them twice.
THE LINEUP (unchanged from v3). generate draws the template uniformly, then the parameter, then a MINIMAL identifying example PAIR (both together leave exactly one rule of U alive, neither alone does; uniqueness 500/500, minimality 500/500; a triple only when no pair works), and then five candidates of one length in which every decoy is matched to the true one in four ways. (a) TRAP PROFILE: all five fire exactly the same set of example-consistent excluded rules, 500/500 -- measured consequence, all 11592 fitted traps over 2000 clues are satisfied by ALL FIVE candidates or by NONE, so no excluded rule and no count of excluded rules separates them. (b) SHAPE: all five use the same number of different letters wherever a group exists, the fallback direction randomised. (c) THE RARITY ORDER: generate carries the attacker's own 627-predicate bank (the union of ospren1a's f_tavrik, ospren1b's word features and dornic1b's tavrik_preds), intersects it over the examples, computes for every candidate the surprise of the RAREST bank predicate that picks it alone, and aims the true candidate's rank in that order at a uniformly random place; (d) the COUNT order and the LETTER-OVERLAP order are aimed the same way. LEVER 0 (choose, among minimal pairs, the one on which the rarest surviving bank predicate ENTAILED by the rule is dullest) is implemented and kept, but it is measured at -0.2 +- 1.8 points here -- inside noise, and NOT claimed as a defence.
DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED (never in U; the decoys' sponsors; mean 5.8 of them fit any one clue): contains every letter the examples share; at least / at most as many vowels as the least / most vowelly example; more consonants than vowels; it starts with a consonant; the 2nd letter is a vowel / a consonant; the same number of letters as the examples; no letter is repeated; the same first letter; it rhymes (same last two letters); two vowels side by side; it ends with a vowel / a consonant. NEWLY EXCLUDED in v4: the first and last letters n apart; a letter comes back after n other letters; the first/last letter is the earliest/latest in the alphabet; "it ends with the next-door letter of the one it starts with" and "two letters in a row are next-door in the alphabet" (both are alphabet-step counting, the same complaint); "every vowel is followed by a consonant" (density .572 -- a lineup cannot carry a rule near .5, four decoys all lacking one property is itself a signature); "the vowels are all the same" (nested inside "the same vowel turns up twice"); "the last vowel is an e" (Jaccard .79 against has_e). Also excluded by construction: anything about LENGTH (all five candidates share one), about SOUND or MEANING, and every LOOSE statement.
WITNESSES over 2000 fresh clues (seeds 1e6..1e6+1999) unless stated: the in-U intersection, i.e. a player who knows U, 100.0 %; the true rule (solve) 100.0 %, and 100.0 % answering by index; THE FULL REVISION-3 ATTACK simulated with the 627-predicate bank (skip-harvest base rates, random-candidate labels, per-predicate unique-explanation weights, rarity-weighted pick; 1500 test clues, mean of 3 disjoint label draws, SE 1.3) 44.6 % at 0 labels, 46.8 at 30, 47.7 at 60, 51.2 at 120, 52.0 at 240 -- against v3's 39.9 / 41.5 / 42.5 / 43.9 / 45.0 under the identical harness; the candidate satisfying the MOST example-consistent bank predicates 27.6 %; the smallest letter-distance to an example 25.1 %; the outlier of the five 22.6 %; the most vowels 21.4 %; a random candidate 21.0 %; pick candidate 1 20.6 %; the alphabetically first 20.5 %; the most different letters 17.9 %; the FEWEST bank predicates 11.8 %; the medoid 12.4 %; a player who knows U minus two templates 85.5-89.4 %. Every EXCLUDED rule followed blindly scores 11.6-22.4 % (all random tie-breaking; the fitted traps are all-or-none by construction). Two RETIRED families still show a shadow, and both shadows are rules of U wearing another hat: "the first and last letters are n apart" scores 73.3 % on the 12 % of clues where it fits, but 100 % of that is the clues whose hidden rule IS "the same letter starts and ends it" (distance 0 is the same sentence) and 19.8 % elsewhere; "the last letter is the latest in the alphabet" scores 37.6 % on 6 % of clues, and that is the ends-with family (y, t, s, r are late letters) at 58.8 % with everything else at chance. The other five retired families score 17.1-24.4 % (n = 30-99).
LEVERS, measured under identical conditions on 1500 test clues at 60 labels (SE 1.3; a difference needs ~3.6 points to clear 2 SE): as shipped 47.4 %; with the three cheap templates at DOUBLE weight 58.1 % (+10.7, the softening dial and the biggest lever in the table); with the decoys UNAIMED 54.6 % (+7.2, 4 sigma); with template 9 "the same letter starts and ends it" dropped 42.8 % (-4.6, the price of the fourth slope template); with k = 4 instead of 5, 50.6 % (+3.2, INSIDE 2 SE -- and a repeat of the whole table gave +1.1, so unlike v3, where the fifth candidate was worth +5.8, it buys nothing measurable against v4's easier universe; k = 5 is kept for pool consistency, not claimed as a defence); with k = 6, 46.2 % (-1.2, noise); with three-example clues 45.8 % (-1.6, noise, exactly as in v3); with lever 0 off 47.2 % (-0.2, noise). Lever 3 (the relational universe itself) is unchanged from v3, where the same attacker scored 98.0 % against v2's universe of cheap predicates.
LEARNING U: with the bank plus the whole of U handed to the attacker (the honest ceiling -- a player who guesses the right vocabulary) the same engine scores 74.7 % at 0 labels, 88.3 at 30, 91.4 at 60, 96.2 at 120, 98.3 at 240, learning 0 / 21 / 44 / 75 / 82 % of U as it goes. With the generic bank alone, coverage can never pass the four slope templates, 17 of the 33 rules and 30 % of clues. The gap 48 % -> 91 % is the class: it is paid for by noticing that the class talks about RELATIONS BETWEEN TWO LETTERS OR TWO PLACES.
SCORE is 894 chars (still needs max_score_code_chars = 1024, the raise RULE_FAMILIES.md sec.4 allows for this paradigm): it splits the clue on the blank line, resolves an ASCII index or a verbatim candidate, rebuilds all 33 rules of U, filters them by the examples, insists on a single survivor and checks that the CHOSEN CANDIDATE obeys it. A word that is not in the lineup scores 0. No hidden channel; words.is_word is not needed at all. Checked candidate-by-candidate against the reference predicate on 600 clues x 5 candidates x 4 answer forms (verbatim, index, upper case with whitespace, spaced index) -- 12000 checks, 0 disagreements -- and it rejects "", "0", "6", "9", "x", "1"*100, "9"*4000, the clue itself, an example word, "hel lo", "elan", the unicode digits, "-1", "1.0", "None", "[1]" and a two-line answer without raising.
DEMOS: "statute / neither" + [sheet tenth taste reset treat] -> reset (4) (the 2nd letter and the 2nd-from-last letter are the same); "nexus / popcorn" + [priest tribal credit smoked priced] -> credit (3) (the vowels go up the alphabet); "allied / roof" + [arrange textile texture expense defense] -> arrange (1) (it has a double letter -- the learnable slope).
PREDICTED: 35-45 % without a demo and 50-65 % with one; mean across two Opus teams ~ 0.45-0.55, i.e. calibrated. The simulator ran ~3 points hot on v3 (42.5 simulated at 60 labels against 39 % measured over four players), so v4's 47.7 / 52.0 at 60 / 240 labels reads as ~44-49 % for a real demo-less Opus centaur. The risk is on the EASY side: U is now 13 templates and a player who spends a demo and says "it is about two letters, or about the vowels" can write it down; if a run comes back above 0.7 the lever to pull is dropping template 9 and the fourth slope template (-5 points), not adding arithmetic back.

VOW = "aeiou"

# --- the universe U, REVISION 4: 13 templates, 33 rules ----------------------
# v4 is a TRIM of v3 for kid legibility (judge: kid 3.83, "half the universe reads like a
# puzzle-book trick rather than a playground observation").  Every COUNTED relation is gone
# -- the exact alphabet distance between the first and last letters, "a letter comes back
# after exactly n other letters", and the four "the first/last letter is the earliest/latest
# in the alphabet" scans.  What is left is nine relations a kid SEES when the two clue words
# are read aloud, plus four templates a generic predicate bank can also express ("the same
# letter starts and ends it", "there is a k in it", "a double letter", "it ends with t"),
# kept on purpose as the learnable slope.
U = [(0, ""), (1, ""), (2, "")] + [(3, c) for c in "aeiou"] + [(4, c) for c in "aiou"] + \
    [(5, ""), (6, ""), (7, ""), (8, ""), (9, "")] + [(10, c) for c in "bfkmpvw"] + \
    [(11, "")] + [(12, c) for c in "dglnrsty"]


def FV(w):
    for c in w:
        if c in VOW:
            return c


def P(r, w):
    """Is word w an instance of rule r?  (the same table the scorer rebuilds)"""
    t, q = r
    h = (len(w) + 1) // 2
    v = [c for c in w if c in VOW]
    k = [c for c in w if c not in VOW]
    return [w[1] == w[-2],                                    # 0  2nd == 2nd from the end
            sum(c in VOW for c in w[h:]) > sum(c in VOW for c in w[:len(w) // 2]),   # 1
            sum(c in VOW for c in w[h:]) < sum(c in VOW for c in w[:len(w) // 2]),   # 2
            FV(w) == q,                                       # 3  first vowel is q
            FV(w[::-1]) == q,                                 # 4  last vowel is q
            any(w.count(c) > 1 for c in v),                   # 5  the same vowel twice
            any(w.count(c) > 1 for c in k),                   # 6  the same consonant twice
            len(v) > 1 and v == sorted(v),                    # 7  vowels up the alphabet
            len(v) > 1 and v == sorted(v)[::-1],              # 8  vowels down the alphabet
            w[0] == w[-1],                                    # 9  starts and ends the same
            q in w,                                           # 10 there is a q in it
            any(w[i] == w[i + 1] for i in range(len(w) - 1)),  # 11 a double letter
            w[-1] == q][t]                                    # 12 it ends with q


def near(x, y):
    """x is y, or one letter changed / added / removed. Keeps the EXAMPLES apart only."""
    if len(x) == len(y):
        return sum(p != q for p, q in zip(x, y)) < 2
    if len(x) > len(y):
        x, y = y, x
    return len(y) - len(x) == 1 and any(y[:i] + y[i + 1:] == x for i in range(len(y)))


# --- what the EXCLUDED (trap) rules read off a word --------------------------
def XFEAT(w):
    """(letter set, #vowels, length, first letter, last two letters, a letter repeats,
        2nd letter is a vowel, two vowels side by side, last letter is a vowel,
        more consonants than vowels)"""
    ls = 0
    for c in w:
        ls |= 1 << (ord(c) - 97)
    nv = 0
    for c in w:
        if c in VOW:
            nv += 1
    return (ls, nv, len(w), w[0], w[-2:], len(set(w)) < len(w), w[1] in VOW,
            any(w[i] in VOW and w[i + 1] in VOW for i in range(len(w) - 1)),
            w[-1] in VOW, (len(w) - nv) * 2 > len(w))


def TRAPS(X):
    """The excluded rules -- never in U -- that are consistent with EVERY example
    (X = the examples' XFEATs). Each is a (code, parameter) pair read by TBITS."""
    t = []
    sh = X[0][0]
    for x in X:
        sh &= x[0]
    if sh:
        t.append((0, sh))                                  # has every letter they share
    t.append((1, min(x[1] for x in X)))                    # >= the least vowelly example
    t.append((2, max(x[1] for x in X)))                    # <= the most vowelly example
    if all(x[9] for x in X):
        t.append((3, 0))                                   # more consonants than vowels
    if all(x[3] not in VOW for x in X):
        t.append((4, 0))                                   # it starts with a consonant
    if all(x[6] for x in X):
        t.append((5, 0))                                   # the 2nd letter is a vowel
    if not any(x[6] for x in X):
        t.append((6, 0))                                   # the 2nd letter is a consonant
    if len(set(x[2] for x in X)) == 1:
        t.append((7, X[0][2]))                             # the same number of letters
    if not any(x[5] for x in X):
        t.append((8, 0))                                   # no letter is repeated
    if len(set(x[3] for x in X)) == 1:
        t.append((9, X[0][3]))                             # the same first letter
    if len(set(x[4] for x in X)) == 1:
        t.append((10, X[0][4]))                            # it rhymes (same last two)
    if all(x[7] for x in X):
        t.append((11, 0))                                  # two vowels side by side
    if all(x[8] for x in X):
        t.append((12, 0))                                  # it ends with a vowel
    if not any(x[8] for x in X):
        t.append((13, 0))                                  # it ends with a consonant
    return t


def TBITS(t, x):
    m = 0
    for k, c in enumerate(t):
        h = c[0]
        if h == 0:
            b = x[0] & c[1] == c[1]
        elif h == 1:
            b = x[1] >= c[1]
        elif h == 2:
            b = x[1] <= c[1]
        elif h == 3:
            b = x[9]
        elif h == 4:
            b = x[3] not in VOW
        elif h == 5:
            b = x[6]
        elif h == 6:
            b = not x[6]
        elif h == 7:
            b = x[2] == c[1]
        elif h == 8:
            b = not x[5]
        elif h == 9:
            b = x[3] == c[1]
        elif h == 10:
            b = x[4] == c[1]
        elif h == 11:
            b = x[7]
        elif h == 12:
            b = x[8]
        else:
            b = not x[8]
        if b:
            m |= 1 << k
    return m



# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# THE ATTACKER'S BANK, rebuilt inside the challenge.  This is the union of the three
# word-predicate banks the Revision-2 players actually brought (ospren1a's f_tavrik,
# ospren1b's word features, dornic1b's tavrik_preds): 199 feature keys, 627 realised
# (key, value) predicates over the pool.  The lineup is aimed against it -- see LINEUP.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
AZ = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
SUF = ("ing", "ed", "er", "ly", "s", "y", "e", "ion", "al", "ful", "ss", "ll", "tt", "pp")
PRE = ("un", "re", "in", "ex", "de", "pro", "con")


def SYL(w):
    n = 0
    p = False
    for c in w:
        v = c in VOW
        if v and not p:
            n += 1
        p = v
    if w.endswith("e") and n > 1:
        n -= 1
    return n


def FEAT(w):
    L = len(w)
    f = {}
    cnt = {}
    for c in w:
        cnt[c] = cnt.get(c, 0) + 1
    nv = sum(1 for c in w if c in VOW)
    rr = []
    for c in w:
        if rr and rr[-1][0] == c:
            rr[-1][1] += 1
        else:
            rr.append([c, 1])
    f["n"] = L; f["n%2"] = L % 2
    f["first"] = w[0]; f["last"] = w[-1]; f["fl"] = w[0] == w[-1]
    f["sv"] = w[0] in VOW; f["ev"] = w[-1] in VOW
    f["nv"] = nv; f["nc"] = L - nv; f["nv%2"] = nv % 2
    f["dbl"] = any(w[i] == w[i + 1] for i in range(L - 1))
    f["rep"] = len(cnt) < L; f["nd"] = len(cnt); f["ndeqL"] = len(cnt) == L
    f["asc"] = list(w) == sorted(w); f["desc"] = list(w) == sorted(w)[::-1]
    f["rare"] = any(c in "jqxz" for c in w); f["rare2"] = any(c in "jqxzkvwy" for c in w)
    f["palin"] = w == w[::-1]
    f["dblvow"] = any(w[i] == w[i + 1] and w[i] in VOW for i in range(L - 1))
    f["dblcon"] = any(w[i] == w[i + 1] and w[i] not in VOW for i in range(L - 1))
    f["adjalpha"] = any(abs(ord(w[i]) - ord(w[i + 1])) == 1 for i in range(L - 1))
    f["y"] = "y" in w
    f["nvowruns"] = sum(1 for i, c in enumerate(w) if c in VOW and (i == 0 or w[i - 1] not in VOW))
    f["maxrun"] = max(n for _, n in rr)
    f["ends_ing"] = w.endswith("ing"); f["ends_ed"] = w.endswith("ed"); f["ends_s"] = w.endswith("s")
    f["firstalpha"] = ord(w[0]) - 96; f["sumalpha"] = sum(ord(c) - 96 for c in w)
    f["vowset"] = tuple(sorted(set(c for c in w if c in VOW)))
    f["onevowtype"] = len(f["vowset"]) == 1
    f["firstlt_last"] = w[0] < w[-1]
    f["2v"] = w[1] in VOW
    f["a2"] = any(w[i] in VOW and w[i + 1] in VOW for i in range(L - 1))
    f["c3"] = any(all(w[i + j] not in VOW for j in range(3)) for i in range(L - 2))
    f["alt"] = all((w[i] in VOW) != (w[i + 1] in VOW) for i in range(L - 1))
    f["halfvow"] = nv * 2 == L; f["moreC"] = (L - nv) * 2 > L
    f["syl"] = SYL(w)

      decoy must have a unique explanation as rare as the truth's -- which is possible only
      because most rules of U are NOT in the bank, so the truth's own explanation is an
      accident of the same kind as the decoys'.
